title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a method to convert categorical data into a numerical format. Each category is represented by a binary vector, where only one element is '1' and the rest are '0'.

title: Why One-Hot Encode Codons?
text: Each codon is a sequence of $$3$$ letters, and there are $$64$$ possible codons. By one-hot encoding each codon, we can capture the unique information each codon provides, which is crucial for understanding the DNA sequence.

title: Compact Representation
text: A compact representation means using the least amount of data to capture the necessary information. One-hot encoding each codon is compact because it uses a fixed size for each codon, regardless of the DNA string length.

hintAnswer: One hot encode each of the 1,000 disjoint codons, per sample.
title: Choosing the Best Encoding Strategy
text: Given the options, which encoding strategy provides a compact representation while preserving the meaning of the data?
choices: Apply one one hot encoding to the entire DNA string.
One hot encode each of the 1,000 disjoint codons, per sample.
One hot encode each of the $$500$$ disjoint $$6$$ letter combinations, per sample.
Bag of words encoding, where each 'word' is a codon
